text: You enter the supermarket, just needing milk. A quick grab and go, that's the plan. Pure efficiency, a simple routine.
But the milk isn't upfront. You walk past produce, snacks, then cleaning supplies. Your 'quick trip' stretches, deeper into the store.
Why this layout? Bad design? Random? You want your milk, but it feels like a deliberate maze, testing patience.
Then it clicks. Essentials like milk and bread are always at the back. It's strategic; stores ensure you pass *every* tempting product.
This system maximizes exposure. Each extra step offers impulse buy chances, transforming your focused mission into a larger, unplanned cart.
Next time you trek to the back, you'll see the journey differently. You're not just shopping; you're navigating an invisible system.
